newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT -FTSE to approach but fall short of 4,800.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT -FTSE to approach but fall short of 4,800.

text.p: The FTSE 100 index is poised to move higher on Friday and approach the 4,800 level, technical analysts said.

Judging by the actions of the past two days, the market seems to have found a near-term floor at 4,730 and it has arrested a downtrend which has been the main influence for much of this week, they added.
But while utilities and cyclical stocks may put in a better performance than shares in the financial sector today, the market is not ready to blast through 4,800 yet.
By 0715 GMT, the FTSE was indicated unchanged at 4,767.8.

Breadth readings for the FTSE on Thursday -- which showed the number of advancing stocks to those declining was 11 to nine -- imply the market has a slightly positive bias but will struggle to go higher.
This is in contrast with the broader market of over 2,000 stocks which had negative breadth on Thursday with five stocks advancing to nine declining.
So the deciding factor on whether the market can end the day on a cheerful note will be the wholesale inflation data from the U.S. which will be released at 1230 GMT, analysts said.
Economists polled by Reuters forecast U.S. producer prices for June will be flat but the market may get a fillip if the data is weaker than expected.
In contrast, if the data shows wholesale price inflation nudging higher, the market will end the day in a depressed state, analysts said.
